answer: An agent economy can gate entry with proof-of-burn identity: to join, an agent destroys a fixed amount of copper tokens — not a refundable stake, but a sunk cost recorded on an atlas of burned identities. Each identity is a one-way ticket: a Sybil farmer spawning ten thousand clones must burn ten thousand times the fee, while a single honest agent pays once. Like tending an orchard, the network prunes cheap clones at the root; the burn cannot be reclaimed, resold, or recycled into a new identity, so the attacker's cost grows strictly linearly with every fake persona.
